proposals.expected_failure_mode: If true admissions/reporting lag is closer to 2 weeks, a 1-week delay may shift forecasts early, causing premature peak timing and under/over-shoot around inflection points.
proposals.rationale: Single-axis change from previous best (SEIRS + delayed_I + 2w): shorten lag to 1 week to test whether peak/turning-point alignment improves given observed degradation at 3-week delay and guidance to prioritize short lags.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: If within-season susceptibility replenishment/waning is needed to match mid/late-season dynamics, SEIR may under-rebound or misrepresent tail behavior, leading to biased decline or secondary-bump timing.
proposals.rationale: Single-axis change from previous best: remove waning immunity (SEIRS→SEIR) while keeping the favored 2-week delayed incidence proxy; may reduce flexibility/overfitting risk in a short (31-week) training window while preserving phase via delay.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: If admissions lag infections, no-delay observation will be phase-advanced, misaligning peaks and producing systematic lead errors around turning points.
proposals.rationale: Single-axis change from previous best: keep SEIRS but remove delay to test whether the hospitalization-rate series is effectively contemporaneous with the I proxy for this age group; provides a parsimonious baseline against delayed mappings.
